newsitem.title: USA: Yacht hopes to break cross-Atlantic record.
newsitem.headline: Yacht hopes to break cross-Atlantic record.

text.p: An 80-foot (25-metre) racing yacht set sail from the coast of New Jersey on Tuesday in an attempt to break a 92-year-old record for sailing across the Atlantic Ocean, a spokesman said.

The Nicorette left at 7:35 a.m. EST (1135 GMT) just ahead of a storm that the captain and crew hoped would help "sling-shot" the boat across the ocean to Lizard Point, England, said spokesman Jeff Blumenfeld.
They aim to break a record set in 1905 by the American schooner Atlantic, which sailed to Lizard Point from Sandy Hook, New Jersey, in 12 days and four hours, he said.
The yacht left in a 10-knot wind under overcast skies ahead of a storm, the spokesman said.
"They were watching the barometer fall," he said. "They were trying to get ahead of this storm."
The crew had hoped for a more powerful storm, such as a hurricane or a so-called nor'easter, a type of gale that hits the northeastern U.S. coast, "but they still have an excellent chance," he said.
They are aiming to make the crossing in eight or nine days, he said.

While other ships with motors or mechanized sail controls have broken the Atlantic's 1905 record, it remains the only non-mechanized monohull record recognised by the World Sailing Speed Racing Council, Blumenfeld said. The Nicorette uses neither motors nor mechanized sail controls, he said.

The head of the 16-person crew on the ultra-light, high-speed yacht is Ludde Ingvall, a Finn who lives in Sweden. The $2.5 million high-tech ship is equipped with advanced computer navigation systems.
The ship is named after Nicorette nicotine gum, a stop-smoking aid manufactured by the yacht's main sponsor, Pharmacia & Upjohn Consumer Healthcare of Helsingborg, Sweden.
